assessments.filename: 2025-Zhou-WYWEB A NLP Evaluation Benchmark For Classical Chinese.md
assessments.short_title: WYWEB: NLP Evaluation Benchmark for Classical Chinese

features.B3_note: Classical Chinese texts treated as undifferentiated cultural heritage; no distinction between Buddhist, Confucian, or Taoist content

assessments.assessor_notes: WYWEB is a general NLP benchmark for classical Chinese text, not a religious values benchmark. Its religious relevance is incidental -- classical Chinese texts happen to include Buddhist and Confucian works, but the benchmark tests NLU tasks (classification, labeling, reading comprehension, translation) not values understanding. A3 scored very low.

assessments.filename: 2024-Cao-C3Bench A Comprehensive Classical Chinese Understanding Benchmark for.md
assessments.short_title: C3Bench: Classical Chinese Understanding Benchmark for LLMs

features.B3_note: Ten domains from classical Chinese lumped together; Buddhist/Confucian/Taoist texts appear in the mix but are not separately analyzed

assessments.assessor_notes: Like WYWEB, C3Bench tests NLU capabilities on classical Chinese (50K text pairs, 5 tasks, 10 domains). Religious content is incidental. The benchmark evaluates classification, retrieval, NER, punctuation, and translation -- not religious values, ethics, or theology.

features.B3_note: Single-tradition (Sunni mainstream) Quranic text with 32 reciters; no denominational comparison

assessments.assessor_notes: Quran-MD is a multimodal dataset (text + audio) of the Quran at verse and word level, supporting ASR, tajweed detection, and TTS. It is a data resource, not a values benchmark. Religious relevance is through the sacred text itself, but the tasks are primarily linguistic/acoustic, not values-oriented.

assessments.filename: 2025-Pramodya-SinhalaMMLU A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Multitask.md
assessments.short_title: SinhalaMMLU: Multitask Language Understanding in Sinhala

features.B3_note: Covers Buddhism, Christianity, Islam, and Catholicism as separate subjects in the Sri Lankan curriculum

assessments.assessor_notes: SinhalaMMLU is an MMLU-style benchmark for Sinhala covering 30 subjects. It includes dedicated religion subjects (Buddhism, Christianity, Islam, Catholicism) from the Sri Lankan curriculum, making it partially relevant to religious values. However, these are knowledge-recall (exam-style) questions, not ethical reasoning. 7000+ questions total but only a fraction are religion-specific.

assessments.short_title: IslamTrust: LLM Alignment with Islamic Values

features.B3_note: Explicitly covers consensus-based positions across Sunni schools of thought; tests interfaith knowledge separately

assessments.assessor_notes: IslamTrust is the strongest Islamic values alignment benchmark in this batch. It directly tests LLM alignment with Islamic ethical principles across 6 domains, using MCQ format in both Arabic and English. Best model achieved only 66.5% alignment. Genuinely tests values, not just knowledge recall. Duplicate with ID 56.

features.B3_note: Single Sunni tradition; no denominational analysis

assessments.assessor_notes: Expanded QA dataset for Quranic passage retrieval. Uses AraElectra and AraBERT fine-tuned on Quranic context. Tests information retrieval from sacred text, not values alignment or ethical reasoning. 251-629 questions.

assessments.short_title: MITRA: Parallel Corpus for Buddhist NLP

features.B3_note: Covers multiple Buddhist canonical languages (Sanskrit, Pali, Chinese, Tibetan) spanning diverse Buddhist traditions

assessments.assessor_notes: MITRA is a massive parallel corpus (1.74M sentence pairs) of Buddhist texts across Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan. Its purpose is machine translation and semantic retrieval for Buddhist literature, not values evaluation. Rich cross-tradition Buddhist coverage but tests NLP capabilities, not values alignment.

assessments.short_title: ByT5-Sanskrit: Unified Model for Sanskrit NLP

features.B3_note: Sanskrit language treated as a single domain; no tradition-specific analysis

assessments.assessor_notes: ByT5-Sanskrit is a pretrained language model for Sanskrit NLP tasks (word segmentation, morphological analysis, dependency parsing, OCR correction). It is a computational linguistics tool, not a religious values benchmark. Religious relevance is purely through the language of Hindu/Buddhist sacred texts.

assessments.short_title: FaithBench: AI Benchmark for Christian Theology

features.B3_note: Covers Biblical Exegesis, Hermeneutics, Systematic Theology, Biblical Canon, Church History across traditions
features.Q1_note: Peer-review quality mentioned but no IAA metric

assessments.assessor_notes: FaithBench is a serious Christian theology benchmark with expert-level multi-hop reasoning questions. No PDF or extract available, so confidence is medium. Six evaluation dimensions spanning exegesis to church history. Anti-gaming design with held-out test cases. Tests deep theological competence, not just knowledge recall. No PDF available to verify claims.

assessments.short_title: SEA-Guard: Multilingual Safeguard for Southeast Asia

features.B3_note: Treats Islam and Buddhism as demographic categories in SEA safety context; e.g. 'assumes all Indonesians are Muslim' as a harmful prompt

assessments.assessor_notes: SEA-Guard is a safety/safeguard model for Southeast Asian cultural contexts. Religion appears as one dimension of cultural sensitivity (e.g., assuming all Indonesians are Muslim), but the benchmark primarily tests safety classification, not religious values alignment. High bias-values conflation score because it treats religion as a demographic sensitivity category.

features.B3_note: Evaluates from evangelical Protestant perspective (Nicene Creed doctrines); 7 theologians graded 7 LLMs
features.Q1_note: 7 theologians graded responses but no formal IAA reported

assessments.assessor_notes: Industry benchmark from The Gospel Coalition. 7 orthodox theologians graded 7 LLMs on most-Googled religious questions. DeepSeek R1 ranked highest. Tests doctrinal reliability from an evangelical Protestant standpoint. Low confidence because the PDF extract was empty (0 pages extracted) and the paper itself is sparse.

assessments.short_title: eBible Corpus: Bible Translation for Low-Resource Languages

features.B3_note: Bible translation treated as a single task; denominational differences in translation not addressed

assessments.assessor_notes: The eBible Corpus is a massive multilingual Bible translation resource on HuggingFace (3000+ languages). It is designed to support machine translation for low-resource languages, not values assessment. The sacred text content is the vehicle for MT, not the evaluation target.

features.B3_note: Focused on Theravada Buddhism (Sinhala/Pali tradition) but notes potential for Zen/Shingon/Pure Land variants

assessments.assessor_notes: BuddhismEval is the first dedicated Buddhist ethical reasoning benchmark for LLMs. Includes factual, ethical, philosophical, and applied reasoning questions drawn from canonical texts and government exam papers. Bilingual (English/Sinhala). No PDF or extract available. Strong values relevance -- explicitly tests Buddhist ethical reasoning, not just knowledge. Confidence medium due to no PDF.

features.B3_note: Sunni hadith science methodology; no cross-school comparison
features.Q1_note: 92.47% F1 reported for the classification model

assessments.assessor_notes: MAHADDAT is the first dataset dedicated to fabricated hadith detection using textual content analysis (Matn). Relevant to religious values because hadith authenticity directly impacts Islamic jurisprudence and practice. However, the task is binary classification (authentic vs fabricated), not values reasoning. BERT achieves 92.47% F1.

features.B3_note: Covers multiple Sikh canonical texts but no internal tradition comparison

assessments.assessor_notes: BaniDB is a community-maintained digital Gurbani database covering SGGS and Dasam Granth. It is a data resource, not a benchmark. Could potentially be used for Sikh knowledge QA but has no evaluation framework. API accessible. Low confidence as no PDF or extract available and this is a community project page.

features.B3_note: Single tradition; world's first Gurbani database with 60 Raags classification

assessments.assessor_notes: GurbaniDB is a search engine and database for the Guru Granth Sahib with 52+ language translations. Data resource, not a benchmark. 2010 community project. No evaluation framework, no test items. Valuable as a Sikh scriptural data source but not usable as a values benchmark in its current form.

features.B3_note: Religion is one of 4 bias dimensions (gender, race, religion, queerness); religious groups treated as demographic labels

assessments.assessor_notes: REDDITBIAS tests bias in conversational models across 4 dimensions including religion. Religion is treated as a demographic category for bias measurement, not as a source of values. Extremely high bias-values conflation (85) -- this is fundamentally a bias detection tool, not a religious values benchmark. Published at ACL 2021.

features.B3_note: Covers Vedas, epics (Mahabharata, Ramayana), and Bhagavad Gita as separate texts

assessments.assessor_notes: DharmicData is a structured JSON collection of Hindu sacred texts (Vedas, Gita, epics). Community project on GitHub. Data resource only, no benchmark or evaluation framework. Could be used for Hindu knowledge QA but has no test items. Open Database License.

features.B3_note: Covers Tafsir and Ahadith domains; no denominational differentiation reported
features.Q1_metric: Human evaluation: model consistency with expert scholars 11-20%, contextual understanding 50-90%

assessments.assessor_notes: 73,000+ QA pairs for Quranic Tafsir and Ahadith domains. Substantial dataset with human evaluation showing model consistency with scholars is only 11-20%. Moderately relevant to values because Islamic QA inherently touches on ethical and juridical reasoning, though framed as information retrieval.

features.B3_note: Vedic Sanskrit treated as a single linguistic corpus; no theological analysis

assessments.assessor_notes: The VCD is a purely linguistic dataset -- annotated compounds from Vedic Sanskrit (ca. 1500-500 BCE). It is a morphological/syntactic resource for computational linguistics, not a values benchmark. Religious relevance is zero despite the Vedic source material. Published at MWE-UD Workshop @ LREC-COLING 2024.

assessments.filename: 2024-So-How AI Trained on the Confucian Analects Can Solve Ethical Dilemmas.md
assessments.short_title: AI Trained on Confucian Analects for Ethical Dilemmas

features.B3_note: Focuses solely on the Analects; no comparison with Neo-Confucianism or other Confucian schools

assessments.assessor_notes: CRITICAL NOTE: The PDF extract appears to be mismatched -- it contains 'Competing Visions of Ethical AI: A Case Study of OpenAI' rather than the Confucian Analects paper. The vault abstract also seems contaminated with OpenAI case study content. Based on the title and DATA_URL, this appears to be a small-scale study training AI on the Analects. Low confidence due to data quality issues. The study concept has genuine values relevance but implementation appears thin.

assessments.filename: 2025-Lahmar-IslamTrust A Benchmark for LLMs Alignment with Islamic Values.md
assessments.short_title: IslamTrust: Benchmark for LLM Alignment with Islamic Values

features.B3_note: Covers consensus across Sunni schools; tests interfaith knowledge separately

assessments.assessor_notes: Duplicate of ID 21 (same paper, slightly different filename). This is the version with full extract read. IslamTrust is the strongest Islamic values alignment benchmark: 6 domains, MCQ, bilingual Arabic/English, consensus-based. Best model only 66.5% aligned. NeurIPS 2025 Muslims in ML workshop. HuggingFace dataset available.

features.B3_note: Uses Schwartz value theory (10 dimensions); religion appears only as a cultural variable, not as a source of ethical content

assessments.assessor_notes: ValueNet is a Schwartz values dataset with 21,374 scenarios in 10 value dimensions. Published at AAAI 2022. It tests general human values for dialogue systems, not specifically religious values. The Schwartz framework includes Tradition and Conformity which tangentially relate to religion, but the benchmark does not engage with any specific religious tradition. rv_islam/christianity/buddhism scores of 50 seem overly generous.

assessments.filename: 2018-Zhao-Finding Answers from the Word of God.md

features.B3_note: Uses Bible trivia questions; no denominational differentiation

assessments.assessor_notes: BibleQA creates a QA dataset from Bible trivia questions, testing answer sentence selection by retrieving relevant Bible verses. Fundamentally an IR/QA task applied to biblical text. Tests factual knowledge about the Bible, not theological reasoning or values alignment. Published at IEEE IJCNN 2018.

assessments.short_title: Similarity Measures in Vedic Sanskrit Literature

features.B3_note: Compares Maitrayani Samhita and Kathaka Samhita, two Vedic schools

assessments.assessor_notes: Digital humanities study using Word2Vec, stylometry, and TRACER for text reuse detection in Vedic Sanskrit. Purely computational linguistics/philology -- analyzes structural alignment between Vedic texts, not values content. A3 is very low despite the sacred source material.

assessments.short_title: Multi-IsnadSet: Sahih Muslim Hadith Graph Dataset

features.B3_note: Sahih Muslim only; no cross-collection or cross-school comparison

assessments.assessor_notes: Graph-structured dataset of multiple Isnad chains for Sahih Muslim hadith. Represents narrator networks as directed graphs. Enables hadith authentication (Sahih/Dhaif classification) via graph analysis. Relevant to Islamic jurisprudence infrastructure but does not directly test values. Data in Brief publication.

assessments.filename: 2024-Multiple Data in Brief-MASAQ Morphologically-Analyzed and Syntactically-Annotated Quran Dataset.md

features.B3_note: Linguistic annotation of Quran text; no theological analysis
features.Q1_note: Expert Arabic linguists using traditional i'rab methodology

assessments.assessor_notes: MASAQ is a morphological and syntactic annotation of the entire Quran with 72 syntactic roles. It is a linguistic resource for NLP (dependency parsing, grammar checking, MT). The Quranic text is the vehicle, but the task is pure computational linguistics. No values content.

assessments.filename: 2024-Nayak-Benchmarking Vision Language Models for Cultural Understanding.md
assessments.short_title: CulturalVQA: Cultural Understanding Benchmark for VLMs

features.B3_note: Tests cultural knowledge (clothing, food, rituals) across 11 countries; religion is one facet among many, not the primary focus
features.Q1_metric: Multiple answers per question (1-5), quality controlled

assessments.assessor_notes: CulturalVQA is a vision-language benchmark testing cultural understanding across 11 countries and 5 continents. 2,378 image-question pairs on clothing, food, rituals, traditions. Religion appears as one cultural facet but is not the primary focus. Disparity found between North America (strong) and Africa (weak). Published at EMNLP 2024. Not a religious values benchmark.

assessments.short_title: QASiNa: Islamic QA on Sirah Nabawiyah

features.B3_note: Focused on Sirah Nabawiyah (Prophet's biography); Sunni perspective

assessments.assessor_notes: QASiNa is an extractive QA dataset for the Sirah Nabawiyah (Prophet's biography) in Indonesian. Evaluates mBERT, XLM-R, IndoBERT, and GPT-3.5/4. The paper explicitly notes that LLMs 'contradict the principles of information transmission' in Islam. Moderately values-relevant because it tests Islamic knowledge authority principles, though the task is extractive QA.

assessments.short_title: Cross-cultural Dataset: Evolution of Religion & Morality

features.B3_note: Explicitly samples from diverse non-WEIRD populations; multiple religious traditions examined as variables
features.Q1_metric: Standardized cross-cultural methods; published in Nature Scientific Data

assessments.assessor_notes: Purzycki et al.'s cross-cultural dataset for the evolution of religion and morality project. Published in Nature Scientific Data. Studies moral behavior across diverse non-WEIRD populations. Genuinely examines religion-morality nexus, but from an anthropological/evolutionary perspective (etic), not within-tradition. High normative pluralism. Not an LLM benchmark but could be adapted.

assessments.filename: 2023-Alyemny-A Data-Driven Exploration of a New Islamic Fatwas.md

features.B3_note: Collected from various trusted agencies, scholars, and websites -- implicitly multi-school

assessments.assessor_notes: FatwaSet is the first public Arabic dataset of Islamic fatwas from authenticated sources. Fatwas are inherently values-laden as they represent Islamic legal/ethical rulings on contemporary issues. High values relevance through the content itself (Islamic jurisprudence), though the dataset is a resource not a benchmark. Appears to be the same as or companion to ID 144.

features.B3_note: Multiple fatwa sources (agencies, scholars, websites)

assessments.assessor_notes: Duplicate/companion to ID 143. Same FatwaSet dataset, same abstract and authors. Likely the dataset description paper vs the analysis paper. Same scores apply.

assessments.filename: 2022-Multiple Data in Brief-Sanadset 650K Data on Hadith Narrators.md

features.B3_note: Sanad data from 926 historical Arabic books; single methodological tradition

assessments.assessor_notes: Sanadset is a large-scale hadith narrator chain dataset (650K entries from 926 books). Enables automated Sanad evaluation for hadith authentication. Infrastructure for Islamic scholarship but not a values benchmark. Usable as Arabic NLP resource. 159,558 hadiths lack Sanads.

features.B3_note: Specifically Catholic; covers Moral Theology, Bioethics, Sacraments, Canon Law, and History/Bias -- all tradition-specific domains

assessments.assessor_notes: CatholicBench tests AI on Catholic theological competence at the intersection of 'rigid dogmatic logic and nuanced pastoral care.' Strong values relevance through Moral Theology and Bioethics dimensions. Measures Pastoral Charity (empathy with truth) and Historical Accuracy (avoiding anti-Catholic tropes). Low confidence because no PDF, no extract, no academic publication -- web-based independent benchmark (catholicbench.com).
